段.meaning: Beside a <part>pole</part> with planks nailed across it, each <part>one</part> a step, a <part>maiden</part> curtseys on every rung as she climbs: up, curtsey, up, curtsey. A teacher ticks a box at each. Reach the top and you've passed the <kanji>grade</kanji>.
段.on: Miss a curtsey and you tumble all the way down to the <sound>dun</sound>geon at the bottom.

終.meaning: A grandmother knits by the fire as <part>winter</part> sets in. The <part>thread</part> runs shorter, the scarf grows longer, and the snow piles up. Last loop, snip. The scarf and the year <kanji>finish</kanji> together.
終.on: She uses the very last bit of thread to sew a button onto a giant <sound>shoe</sound>.
終.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, at last!' she says, and puts her needles down.

点.meaning: A <part>fortune telling</part> lady drips candle wax over <part>hot coals</part> and stares at where it lands. 'A dot here means love, a dot there means money.' Every future is in one tiny <kanji>spot</kanji>.
点.on: A <sound>ten</sound>or bursts in singing, and a drop of wax lands right on the tip of his nose.
点.kun: The smoke makes her sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', which blows out the candle, so she has to light it again.

楽.meaning: On a <part>tree</part> stand sits a big <part>white</part> drum, with two little cymbals of <part>ice</part> tinkling at its sides. Boom, ting, ting! The whole forest starts to dance. It's <kanji>music</kanji>.
楽.on: A <sound>gag</sound>gle of geese honks along to the beat.
楽.kun: '<sound>Tah</sound>-dah!' says the drummer, ready to stop. '<sound>No</sound>, more!' yells the crowd. This is too much fun.

助.meaning: You're carrying one heavy box, and <part>moreover</part> there are ten more stacked in the van. A neighbour flexes a big <part>muscle</part>, grabs the whole pile and carries it all upstairs. Now that's <kanji>help</kanji>.
助.on: A passing <sound>jo</sound>gger stops to help too, and runs up the stairs with a box under each arm.
助.kun: To say thanks, you hand them both a <sound>tu</sound>b of <sound>su</sound>shi.

正.meaning: A gymnast cartwheels down the mat and has to <part>stop</part> dead on the chalk mark, arms held out flat as a <part>one</part>. She lands without a wobble, toes right on the line, exactly as the rulebook says. The judges raise their cards: <kanji>correct</kanji>.
正.on: Her prize, a shiny gold medal, has been locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe until the scores came in.
正.kun: '<sound>Tah</sound>-<sound>dah</sound>!' she cries, waving her medal at the cheering crowd.
